NOT A BUG -- I filed this on a bad comparison and am closing it rather than leaving a false P1 against the harness.

What I did: compared the CSV's per-question token sum (1,396,799) against the adapter's session_cost_summary prompt_tokens (804,825) and called the 1.73x gap an over-count.

Why that was wrong: they measure different things. usage_metadata.prompt_token_count reports the CONTEXT SIZE AT THAT MOMENT (the prompt_curve climbs 4,399 -> 22,415 monotonically over 103 events). The adapter sums that per event because you ARE billed for the entire context on every turn -- with no caching on the Live API (measured, 89mt), a 22k-token context costs 22k input tokens every single turn. The CSV's per-modality totals are the same accounting seen through the tracker deltas.

The uneven per-modality ratios I cited as evidence (text_in 1.81x, audio_in 1.46x, audio_out 0.80x) are explained by the same thing: text input is the part that grows with context, audio input does not, and audio OUTPUT is per-turn only -- so they cannot share a ratio.

The real finding stands and is recorded in the findings doc instead: per-turn cost RISES steadily across a form (second half costs ~2.1x the first half per field) because the re-billed context grows and nothing evicts it. That is a product-cost fact, not an instrumentation defect.

No historical figure is retracted on this basis. My claim that the I-90 pitch numbers were inflated ~1.7x was wrong and I have withdrawn it.
